description:
FILED s405 (Opus 5) while shipping #340 (try/catch/finally).  RULED s406 interim (plan-post-s400 §2c): DO NOT START — the layer question is answered at the next review; the default if nothing is said is (a), a not-supported.md entry only.

The spelling most real code uses to enable perl 5.34's try/catch fails twice:

1. PPI does not switch its `try` support on for `use experimental 'try'` —
   only for `use feature`.  So the construct lexes like the no-pragma case
   (one swallowing statement) and the file does not compile.
2. experimental.pm itself dies at load under PCL: it does
   `$_ = version->new($_) for values %min_version;` and `for values %h` does
   NOT alias in PCL — the write lands on a copy, the hash keeps its strings,
   and the next line calls ->stringify on "5.34.0".  Probed:
   `$_ = $_ * 10 for values %h` leaves %h untouched (perl: multiplied); the
   ARRAY form aliases correctly.

(2) is the `values` half of the residue fable-answers-s370 §5 records, which is
RULED onto the E5 boxed-aggregates axis (DO NOT START).  A lib/experimental.pm
workaround shim (the File::Basename / IO::Handle pattern, with a delete-when
trigger) would fix (2) for every `use experimental` program, but not (1).

`use feature 'try'` works today and is what Pl/t/try-catch-01.t and op/try.t
use; this task is about the other spelling.


RULED s407 (fable-answers-s406.md Â§4.7 ask 3, Â§5.1) â LAYER ANSWER = (c'),
WIDENED.  A feature-enabling CORE pragma is LANGUAGE (feature/experimental/the
`use vN` bundles are perl's own; strict/warnings/utf8 are already known by name),
and the mechanism is NOT a source rewrite: PPI HAS THE HOOK â
  PPI::Document->new(\$src, custom_feature_include_cb => sub { my ($inc)=@_; ... })
is consulted FIRST by PPI::Statement::Include::feature_mods (PPI 1.291).  So
Parser.pm::_ppi_parse (the ONE construction site) passes a callback answering
from a small table of perl's core spellings:
  * `use feature LIST`        -> {try=>'perl'} for 'try', signatures likewise (PPI already)
  * `use experimental LIST`   -> same for try (PPI knows only signatures there)
  * `use vN` / `use N.NNN`    -> the BUNDLE: try for >= 5.040 (NOT 5.036 â perl's
                                 :5.36 bundle has no try), signatures for >= 5.036
  * `no feature 'try'` / `no experimental 'try'` -> {try=>0}
NEW SHAPE found by the review (F1): `use v5.40; try {â¦} catch ($e) {â¦} print
"after\n";` is a WHOLE-STATEMENT DROP today (announced on stderr, rc 0) â PPI's
version hack knows only signatures.  Guard rows: `use v5.40; try`, `use
experimental 'try'`, `use feature 'try'` (already), and a `no feature 'try'`
inverse where `try` is a plain sub name (Try::Tiny shape must keep working:
`try {â¦} catch {â¦};` with the feature OFF).
CAUSE (2), experimental.pm dying at load (`for values %h` does not alias â E5
axis, do not touch): the thin lib/experimental.pm SHIM (module layer, 9a):
import = feature->import(@names) + warnings->unimport("experimental::$_") â both
no-ops here today; unimport symmetric.  Delete-when: `for values %h` aliases.
STRING-EVAL INHERITANCE of the feature is #364 (its own piece).
Bar: gate rows above; corpus-diff (must be IDENTICAL: no population file uses the
new spellings â verify, do not assume); op/try.t unchanged (23/28); a probe of
each spelling vs perl 5.40.3.


DONE s408 (Opus 5).  BOTH causes closed.

(1) THE PPI HALF, exactly as ruled: Pl::Parser::_pcl_feature_include_cb, passed
to PPI::Document->new from _ppi_new -- the ONE construction site, so the first
parse and the post-repair reparse cannot drift.  Answers `use/no feature`,
`use/no experimental` and the `use vN` / `use N.NNN` BUNDLES.  Two refinements
the ruling did not spell out, both measured:
  * a version bundle REPLACES the scope feature set, so the OFF answers are
    explicit (`use feature try; use v5.36;` leaves try off, as perl does);
  * an argument OUTSIDE the table returns an EMPTY hashref, not undef.  Falling
    through would hand `use experimental defer` back to PPI, whose experimental
    branch answers `signatures => 0` for ANY list -- silently disabling
    signatures an earlier line switched on.
Thresholds are STATIC (PCL must compile `use v5.40; try` the same way whatever
perl it runs under) and re-derived from the running perl by a guard row, so a
drift is a red row: try is in perls bundles 5.39/5.40, signatures from 5.35.
version.pm is deliberately NOT used -- lib/ carries a version.pm SHIM and the
transpiler must not depend on which its own /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 finds first (verified: `perl
-Ilib -e 'require Pl/Parser.pm'` fails on the shim).

(2) lib/experimental.pm SHIM, with the delete-when trigger as a GUARD ROW that
fails when `for values %h` starts aliasing.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL 111; emission-ab lib 21/21 SAME and over perls
OWN t/ 560/560 SAME (the claim that matters for a lexer change: no existing
file's emission moves).  op/try.t unchanged 23/5.  NOTHING in either population
uses `use experimental` except op/taint.t, which is TRANSPILE-FAIL for an
unrelated cause (#342 piece 2, the s///e replacement) -- re-checked directly.
Guards: Pl/t/feature-pragma-01.t (22 rows, three layers) + a canary in
misc-fixes-02.t.  Rule 13: ppi-upstream-bugs.md S20 + Bug 17 (three failing
rows) in docs/ppi-bug-report.t.

FOLLOW-ON: #364 (string-eval feature inheritance) is the remaining piece and
now has its prerequisite -- the site can detect `use v5.40` through this table.
